resources.string: The calendar your Boox tablet deserves

BooxDay started with a simple wish: a calendar that truly belongs on an e-ink device. We fell in love with Boox tablets — the paper-like display, the wacom-grade stylus — but kept reaching for our phones to manage schedules. That didn\'t feel right.\n\nAfter waiting for a solution that never came, we built what we wished existed: a planner designed for e-ink with stylus-optimized UI, zero animations, and handwriting integration. This is the first calendar with native Boox SDK integration and the first to integrate with Boox Notes.

BooxDay is built by a solo developer as a labor of love, and is now free and open source. The author uses BooxDay every single day — juggling life as a professional, student, husband, father, and community contributor.

One rule from the start: no calendar without stylus support. The paper-like writing experience is why we buy e-ink tablets.

We believe exceptional hardware deserves equally exceptional software built with genuine care for users. We're fans first, developers second. Every feature asks one question: "Does this make the Boox experience better?"
BooxDay is free and made by one person. If it makes your days easier, you can buy me a coffee. It doesn\'t buy support or features, and BooxDay stays free for everyone either way.

Your memos, tasks and calendar are stored on this tablet. BooxDay has no server and sends nothing to its developer.\n\nThe app goes online to download Google\'s handwriting model (recognition then runs on the tablet) and for what you turn on: calendar sync talks directly to Google or Microsoft, Drive backup goes to your own Google Drive, AI features send only what you use them on to OpenRouter, on your own account, and indexing (Settings → Boox Notes) sends memo and Boox Notes pages to OpenRouter to be read for search. With AI Features off (Settings → AI Settings), none of your data goes to OpenRouter.
